description: Use this when a seller asks whether they must register for VAT or sales tax in a place, for example "I sell e-books from Germany and made 14,000 EUR to buyers in France, do I need to register?", "my US company sells SaaS and has 150,000 USD of sales to Texas, do I owe sales tax there?", "do I need to charge UK VAT on 100,000 GBP of sales to UK customers?". Pass seller_country, buyer_place (an EU country code, GB, or a US state written US-TX or by name), product_kind (physical_goods, digital_products or saas) and yearly_sales in the money of the buyer place (EUR, GBP or USD; leave it out when unknown); add yearly_transactions for US states that also count sales. Returns must_register (yes, no or unclear), the registration limit and what it counts, the standard rate, how often returns are due, where to register, the reasons, and for every answer the official source links with the day each page was read, plus a note that this is not tax advice. Covers the 27 EU member states (One Stop Shop limit of 10,000 EUR), the United Kingdom and 14 US states; any other place returns not_covered with the list of places covered. It does not give advice, does not cover sales to businesses, reduced rates, local taxes or a seller's own-country limit inside the EU, and it does not file or register anything.

buyer_place.description: Where the buyers are: an EU country code (FR, DE, EL for Greece), GB, or a US state written US-TX or by name (Texas). A bare two-letter code is a country, so CA is Canada and California is US-CA.

currency.description: Optional. The currency of yearly_sales. If it differs from the buyer place, the answer asks you to convert; it never guesses a rate.

product_kind.description: physical_goods, digital_products (downloads such as e-books, music or apps) or saas (software used online).

seller_country.description: Where the seller is established: a two-letter country code such as DE, GB, US or VN, or the country name.

yearly_sales.description: Optional. Sales to consumers in the last 12 months, in the money of the buyer place: EUR for the EU, GBP for the UK, USD for a US state. For an EU seller selling to another EU country, send the total to all other EU countries together. If the user gave no figure, leave this out (never send 0 as a stand-in): the answer then states the limit and asks for the figure.

yearly_transactions.description: Optional. Number of sales in the last 12 months. A few US states also count sales, not only dollars.

name: tax_duty

covered.description: With not_covered: the places the table covers.

data_checked.description: The newest day any row of the table was checked.

filing.description: How often and by when returns are due.

must_register.description: Whether the seller has to register to collect VAT or sales tax for this place.

rate.description: standard_percent and what the rate leaves out.

sources.description: Official pages the answer comes from, each with the day it was checked.

stale_data.description: True when a row of the table is older than the age limit.

status.description: ok, not_covered (place not in the table; see covered), currency_mismatch or invalid.

threshold.description: The registration limit that applies, with what is counted. Null when there is none.

title: Check VAT or sales tax registration duty
